title: SLO signal lifecycle playbook and cross-team scrumlog (Q4 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This working playbook defines the lifecycle for SLO signals from hypothesis → definition → instrumentation → validation → experiment → production enforcement. It also captures a cross-team scrumlog (decisions, blockers, notes) for the Q4 2026 SLO initiative so partners (Product, Serving Runtime, Platform Eng, DevEx, CS) have a single source of truth for rollout mechanics and open questions.

Scope:
- Core model-serving endpoints (hosted API, dedicated pools) and the Redwood Console routes that surface latency/cost to customers.
- Signal types: latency percentiles, error-rate (class-based), saturation (queue length/GPU util), and quality-regression signals (from eval pipelines).
- Excludes: batch offline jobs and experiments targeted only at Research sandbox.

High-level goals (Q4):
- Create an SLO signal catalog with owners and instrumentation status for top 12 production routes (target by Nov 1).
- Run 3 staggered canary rollouts with guardrails integrated into the console and ops runbooks.
- Reduce detection-to-remediation median time for Sev2 incidents caused by serving regressions from 47m to <20m.

Success metrics (how we measure progress):
- Coverage: % of Top-12 routes with fully instrumented SLOs and automated alerts >= 90%.
- Alert quality: False positive rate < 15% for SLO alerts during the pilot window.
- Productivity: Median time from a detected SLO breach to runbook start < 12 minutes (measured in incident logs).
- Customer impact: Number of customer-facing incidents attributed to serving regressions down by 30% vs baseline (Q3 2026).

Signals mapping (short):
- Latency: P50/P95/P99 on request-to-first-response and request-to-commit token. Instrumentation: edge-tracing + per-model token timestamps. Owner: Ethan Park (serving-runtime).
- Errors: classification by type (inference-exception, timeout, upstream-400). Instrumentation: structured error codes, sample payloads stored for 24h. Owner: Marta Alvarez (platform-eng).
- Saturation: queue depth + per-GPU active-streams. Instrumentation: exporter + Prom histograms. Owner: Ravi Kapoor (infra).
- Quality regressions: eval-run delta > threshold on curated prompt sets. Instrumentation: nightly eval job + anomaly detector. Owner: Sasha Ilyin (applied-ml).

Minimum Acceptable Definition (example):
- Route: /v1/generate-redwood-medium
- SLO: Availability 99.5% (monthly), Latency P95 < 220ms (95% of requests)
- Alert: Rolling 5m breach of >1.5x error budget burn rate triggers PagerDuty SEV2 + Slack #sre-model-serving

Rollout plan (4-week cadence repeated per route group):
- Week 0: Stakeholder alignment + instrumentation tickets created (owners assigned).
- Week 1: Implement exporters & traces, store schema in observability repo, smoke test on staging.
- Week 2: Backfill historical signals (where possible), run dry-run alerting (notify only Slack).
- Week 3: Canary enforcement: enable PagerDuty routing + automated fallback policy on breach; collect metrics and feedback; decide to promote/reroll.

Sprint-level tasks (examples):
- ENG: Add P99 timing to request logs and shape batching telemetry (PR: observability#298). Due: 2026-10-14. Owner: Ethan.
- PLAT: Expose per-route queue depth metric via exporter. Due: 2026-10-18. Owner: Marta.
- SRE: Author runbook snippets (play, rollback, fallback-to-smaller-model). Due: 2026-10-20. Owner: Leah.
- ML: Curate 120 prompt eval set, build alert thresholds for quality drift. Due: 2026-10-25. Owner: Sasha.

Roles & RACI (condensed):
- Product (caters to customers): R - define acceptable customer-facing thresholds; C - signoff on SLOs.
- Eng-serving-runtime: A - implement timing + tracing; R - change execution.
- Platform/Infra: R - exporter + metrics plumbing; C - capacity planning.
- SRE: A - oncall policy and runbooks; R - alert configuration and response.
- Applied ML: R - quality signal design and evals.

Runbook snippets (copyable):
- Trigger: P95 breach for 10m OR sudden error-rate multiplier > 3x baseline
- Immediate steps: 1) Post to #ops-model-serving with incident tag 2) Run quick health-check script (./scripts/serving-health.sh) 3) If degradation persists > 15m, execute automated traffic split to fallback pool (policy id: TF-73).

Experiment matrix (to test alerting and enforcement):
- A: Dry-run alerts (Slack only) for 2 weeks on Group A routes.
- B: Canary enforcement with automated fallback (50% traffic) for single riskier route.
- C: Full enforcement on low-risk routes with rollback automation.
Metrics collected per experiment: precision/recall of alerts, MTTR, customer error reports.

Risk register (top 6):
- Risk: Alert storm during rollout could overwhelm oncall. Mitigation: Rate-limit alerts; use rolling-window suppression for duplicate signals. Owner: SRE.
- Risk: Missing schema changes break telemetry. Mitigation: Contract tests in CI for observability schema; gate merges. Owner: Eng DevEx.
- Risk: Noise from downstream services interpreted as serving problems. Mitigation: Add causal tagging in traces; correlation dashboard. Owner: Platform Eng.

Outstanding decisions / TODOs:
- Decide default error-budget cadence (hourly vs 5m rolling) for console visualization (ACTION: Product + SRE).
- Finalize fallback model families and capacity reservation policy for canaries (ACTION: Platform + Serving).
- Agreement on retention and sampling for payload traces (privacy + cost tradeoff) (ACTION: Security & Privacy).

Communication plan (brief):
- Weekly SLO sync meeting (Wed 10:00 PT) — publish notes to Confluence page CONFLUENCE-1234.
- Slack channels: #sre-model-serving (ops), #prod-slo (product questions), #observability (implementer discussion).
- Exec updates: Biweekly one-pager summarizing coverage and a11y to execs (send to Leah & VP Eng).

Checklist before full enforcement (must pass all):
- Automated alerts in place + test alert fireworked (yes/no).
- Runbook validated by 2 oncall rotations.
- Fallback pools have capacity tested at 2x expected canary load.
- Security review for trace retention and sampled payloads.

Short scrumlog (selected entries):
- 2026-10-05: Kickoff — owners assigned.
- 2026-10-11: Platform exported per-route queue metric; discovered naming inconsistency (resolved 10/12).
- 2026-10-18: Dry-run alerts enabled for Group A; observed 22% false positives due to transient GC — filter added 10/19.
- 2026-10-28: Canary enforcement trial 1: rollback executed automatically based on error budget — successful.
- 2026-11-02: Product requested lowering P95 threshold for certain low-latency customers; added as experimental parameter.

Notes to self / working thoughts:
- We should consider a single SLO registry (yaml) in repo with small schema; use it to generate docs and CI tests.
- Explore a lightweight machine-learning signal deduplicator for alert noise in early 2027.

References / links (working):
- Observability repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/298
- Jira epic: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SRE-412
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/SLO+Playbook+Draft

Open questions for the next sync:
1) Which product routes are considered "Top-12"; final list by Product by 2026-11-05?
2) How to handle model-variant specific SLOs vs route-level SLOs? (need a simple hierarchy)
3) Can DevEx commit to schema contract tests this sprint?

If you are reading this and own a bullet above — ping me (Leah) in Slack or update this doc with a small note under the scrumlog.

-- end of draft playbook (Q4 2026) --
